step1.title: The model
step1.heading: Requirements in, releases out
step1.lead: CodeFlow turns a software delivery into a standard pipeline: AI members handle analysis, coding, testing and handoff automatically, roles hand off to each other. You only do two things — clarify requirements and accept the result.
step1.callout: Key idea: AI members don't work inside the browser — they are driven by a runner you deploy. Let's bri
step1.roles: Your role: make the requirement clear before work starts (clarify), review the outcome after (accept). Everything in between is tracked, retryable and replayable.
step1.calloutTitle: Key idea: where AI members run
step1.f1d: File a story in ZenTao; it lands in CodeFlow within 60 seconds as a work item
step1.f2d: Analysis → coding & tests → delivery, step by step through the Pipeline with full artifact and log trails
step1.f3d: The reviewer takes over automatically, sends findings back for rework, converges until it passes
step1.f4d: After acceptance the item flows to Released and results are written back to ZenTao — loop closed

step2.title: Bring an executor online
step2.heading: Bring an executor online (required)
step2.lead: An executor is a small daemon on your machine that receives dispatches, calls the model, and reports results back to the platform.
step2.s1: Register an executor on the Executors page to get its ID and token;
step2.s2: On any machine that can reach the platform and a model endpoint, set the environment variables below;
step2.s3: Start the daemon and come back — when the badge turns green you're set.
step2.onlineDesc: All set. Continue to the next step, or go deliver your first work item.
step2.offlineDesc: Follow the three steps below — this page probes every 3 seconds and turns green automatically.
step2.h1Desc: Click below to open the Executors page and create one — the platform issues the token via a simple form.
step2.h2Title: ② Copy the platform-generated launch command
step2.h2Desc: Back on the Executors page, open 'Launch command' for that executor — token, URL and parameters are generated for you. One click to copy.
step2.h3Title: ③ Paste & run, watch it turn green
step2.h3Desc: Paste the command into a terminal on the target machine. The daemon connects automatically — this page turns green when it's online.
step2.cmdTitle: Launch command for '{{name}}' (platform-generated, includes token & parameters)
step2.cmdError: Failed to generate the launch command. Please operate from the Executors page.
step2.cmdHint: No manual environment variables needed — token and platform URL are already in the command.
step2.noExecutorDesc: Click '① Register an executor' above to start; the launch command appears here automatically after registration.
step2.noWorkspaceDesc: You opened this page directly — the probe needs a workspace context. Pick one from the workspace list and this step will continue automatically.
step2.s1d: Executors page → New → save the form. The platform issues the token automatically.
step2.s2d: Open 'Launch command' for that executor — token, URL and parameters are generated. One click to copy; no manual env vars.
step2.s3d: The only terminal step; the daemon connects back automatically and the badge turns green.

step2.online: Executor online — nice! Click Next to continue
step2.hint: Model endpoint: any Anthropic-compatible service works (MiniMax / Claude / GLM / …).

step3.title: Meet the preset squad
step3.heading: A preset squad, ready out of the box
step3.lead: The system ships with a minimal working lineup — your first work item can run right now.
step3.agentDesc: Full-stack Dev (code & tests) + Code Reviewer (browser-level verification), each with its own role.
step3.sdlcDesc: Dev Pipeline and Code-review Pipeline, with step gates and artifact requirements preconfigured.
step3.customLead: Want to customize? All optional — none of it blocks your first delivery:
step3.squadBodyDesc: Squad-based delivery: development hands off to an independent code review automatically; failures loop back for rework.
step3.keyTag: ALL PRESET, READY OUT OF THE BOX

step4.title: Connect your requirement source
step4.heading: Plug in ZenTao, requirements flow in
step4.lead: Once bound, external requirements/defects are pulled in automatically (≤60s polling) and delivery results are written back — a full closed loop.
step4.s1: Prepare a ZenTao integration account (can read products & stories);
step4.s2: Create a binding on the Integrations page: ZenTao URL + account token + product ID, then test the connection;
step4.s3: Bind a product, file a story in ZenTao, and watch it appear here automatically.
step4.s1d: Any account that can read products and stories
step4.s2d: Integrations page → New binding: ZenTao URL + token + product ID → test connection
step4.s3t: File a story, watch it appear
step4.s3d: File a story in ZenTao; it appears in the work-item list within 60 seconds

step4.optionalNote: Skipping is fine: create a work item manually to try a delivery — ZenTao can be connected any time.
